data.narrative:
QunaSys is a Series B quantum computing company founded by Tennin Yan that has raised $33M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 entities across quantum computing—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $63M implied valuation, derived by applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression to the $33M raised proxy. Peer-median valuation cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector; while 5 peers exist in the broader sector, none meet the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints when filtered by stage and tier proximity. Relying on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given stage and maturity variance across the comp set.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $53M (low) to $72M (high) with a median point of $63M. Key uncertainties include the absence of calibrating peer multiples on metrics like ARR or customer concentration, as well as the nascent and heterogeneous stage distribution within quantum computing private markets. The range reflects typical Series B progression mechanics rather than market comparability anchors, warranting supplementary diligence on technical differentiation and customer traction.
